newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money eases on better supply.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money eases on better supply.

text.p: Indian call money ended Monday in the 4.25-5.50 percent range, down from opening quotes of 6.0-6.25 percent on improved funds supply, dealers said.
They said call money rates dropped as liquidity had improved following a cut in banks' cash reserve ratio requirements to 10.5 percent from 11 percent.
"This reduction has released about 21 billion rupees to the banking system," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "There was little demand for funds today with even usual borrowers absent."
Dealers said prices of government securities fell in moderate trade on profit-taking by some market participants.

"With call money coming down, one would normally expect security prices to rise," said a dealer. "But they came down by around five paise. Some market players seem to have booked profits at higher levels today and this caused prices to fall."
The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock traded on Mondya at 102.90 rupees while the 13.55 percent 2001 traded at 101.15, dealers said.
No trades were reported in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
